principles: Candidate repro evidence is useful only before story creation and must remain non-production evidence until later gates consume validated story evidence.
Reuse existing Lattice lifecycle gates instead of introducing a parallel story lifecycle.
Make every proof-looking output immutable, digest-addressed, and explicit about its candidate-only scope.
Keep the first implementation small enough to verify with deterministic smoke tests.
drivers: Reduce repeated story rework by proving failures and spike paths before formal development.
Avoid creating another ungoverned metadata surface that could later be mistaken for DONE proof.

options.name: A: local candidate-only evidence service plus thin CLI commands
pros: Keeps candidate artifacts out of production DONE gates
Can be verified with focused smokes
cons: Does not yet provide full admissibility ledger or Authority quorum

options.name: B: implement full Proof Admissibility contract together with Repro-first
pros: Would provide stronger end-to-end proof semantics immediately
cons: Too broad for this story and likely to destabilize existing lifecycle gates

options.name: C: document-only runbook with no CLI support
cons: Does not solve the host-neutral repeatability problem and leaves evidence capture manual

chosen: A: local candidate-only evidence service plus thin CLI commands
rationale: Option A gives the user a real Repro-first workflow now while preserving existing story lifecycle gates and avoiding premature full admissibility enforcement in the same change.

preMortem.scenario: Candidate artifacts are later treated as DONE evidence by mistake.
preMortem.trigger: A handler or gate accepts a repro-probe or spike artifact as production proof.
preMortem.consequence: The system could ship based on pre-story exploratory evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Mark candidate artifacts with evidenceScope=candidate-only and add smoke tests proving they are not production/DONE admissible.

preMortem.trigger: The new handler writes story files directly instead of calling the existing story_create handler.
preMortem.consequence: New stories could miss background, scope, lock, dedup, or lifecycle metadata protections.
preMortem.mitigation: Reuse createStoryCreateHandlers(ctx).story_create and add a smoke proving a story id is produced through normal story_create output.

preMortem.scenario: Evidence storage creates mutable or ambiguous proof surfaces.
preMortem.trigger: Artifacts are overwritten by id or lack digest/object separation.
preMortem.consequence: A later host cannot audit what was actually reviewed.
preMortem.mitigation: Store immutable JSON objects by sha256 digest, store refs separately, and include strict candidate stage/status fields in outputs.

preMortem.scenario: Red test failure is environmental noise rather than the product bug.
preMortem.trigger: The repro artifact records only a failing command without expected failure pattern or bootstrap prerequisite notes.
preMortem.consequence: Teams could create stories from invalid repros and waste time.
preMortem.mitigation: Require expected failure pattern/observed output fields and expose a reviewer status before story creation.
